title: Milnor exact sequence for a derived inverse limit

from.place: proof, first step, cohomology of the derived inverse limit

statement: Let $(K_n)_{n\geq0}$ be a countable inverse system in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and let $R\varprojlim_nK_n$ be a derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit]. For every integer $i$ there is a natural short exact sequence $$0\to R^1\varprojlim_n H^{i-1}(K_n)\to H^i(R\varprojlim_nK_n)\to\varprojlim_n H^i(K_n)\to0,$$ where $R^1\varprojlim$ denotes the first derived functor of the inverse-limit functor on abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), displayed short exact sequence; More on Algebra, Remark 15.88.5 (Tag 07KY)

proof.text: Construct the right-hand map explicitly: the composite of p and every product projection is compatible with successor transitions, since p(1-s)=0 in a distinguished triangle. Apply cohomology and NatTrans.ofOpSequence to form the cone, then use limit.lift. Set this map to zero on nondistinguished triples. Its projection equations hold by the limit universal property.
The projection-surjectivity lemma makes this chosen map epi. Choose the natural left-hand injection from the connecting-map factorization, mono and exact before the product of cohomology.

The map j from the inverse limit to the product of cohomology is mono by limit extensionality. Its composite with b is H^i(p) followed by the product comparison, by the projection equations. Cancel j to prove ab=0. Use ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono with identity left and middle components and right component j to transfer middle exactness. Mono a and epi b give ShortExact. The left square is furnished by the boundary lemma; the right square follows from the p square after each limit projection, hence by limit extensionality.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07KY and Tag 07KW, with the projection half implemented and boundary half split off
